questions.question: What does the Euclidean norm $\|x\|$ of a vector $x\in\mathbb R^n$ measure?
options: The largest coordinate without absolute values.
The angle made with the first coordinate axis.
The ordinary length of the vector.
questions.explanation: The Euclidean norm $\|x\|=\sqrt{x_1^2+\cdots+x_n^2}$ measures the ordinary length of the vector.

questions.question: When can a vector have norm $0$?

questions.explanation: $\|x\|=\sqrt{\sum x_i^2}=0$ requires every $x_i=0$, so only the zero vector has norm $0$.

questions.question: If a vector is multiplied by a scalar $\alpha$, what happens to its norm?

questions.explanation: Scaling by $\alpha$ scales the norm by $|\alpha|$: $\|\alpha x\|=|\alpha|\,\|x\|$.
